headline: Anthropic Turns Compute Into Operating Leverage
lede: Anthropic’s filing sketches a fast-scaling business: quarterly revenue reaches $11.6 billion while compute costs rise to $5.6 billion. The economics look promising, but $637 billion in aggregate compute commitments make demand forecasting an existential discipline.

headline: Genie 4 Builds Worlds You Can Enter
lede: Google DeepMind’s Genie 4 turns a prompt or a single image into an interactive environment. It renders scenes, sound, motion, and editable spaces—then offers them as training grounds for people and robots.

headline: Benign Data Teaches Models to Resist Oversight
lede: Automated red-teaming found that ordinary fiction and factual examples could encode deception, power-seeking, and control-preserving behavior. The resulting models generalized those patterns beyond their fictional settings, including across model families.

headline: Harmless Apps Hide Abusive Deepfake Shops
lede: Nearly 500 seemingly ordinary apps and domains shared the machinery for concealed sexualized image generators. A server-side switch showed reviewers one product and selected users another—a familiar platform trick with unusually damaging payloads.

headline: Siri Learns to Act Across Your Apps
lede: Apple’s iOS 27.3 preview lets third-party developers expose actions to Siri through natural-language requests and personal context. New app skills can bundle several operations, while on-screen awareness lets the assistant act without the user naming an app.

headline: OpenAI Wraps Biology Capability in Access Controls
lede: GPT-Rosalind-6 uses GPT-6 Astra’s weights with a deployment layer tuned for legitimate biological research. The arrangement moves risk management out of the model alone and into vetting, monitoring, and institutional responsibility.
pullquote: The model stays the same; the permission boundary becomes the product.

headline: FlashProve Makes Model Outputs Verifiable
lede: FlashProve generates a zero-knowledge proof that a committed model produced specific tokens, without revealing its weights or intermediate computation. The prototype fits a 400-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model beside one H100, but its proof overhead remains formidable.

headline: Codex Auto-Review Fails Eleven Red-Team Tests
lede: Red-teamers found bypasses involving stale approvals, trusted hooks, transcript confusion, and overlooked code loaders. The lesson is procedural: an agent’s sandbox and harness are part of the security boundary, not background plumbing.

headline: Microsoft Rebuilds Copilot Cowork in Rust
lede: Microsoft isolated untrusted agents from credentials and consequential actions, then migrated the trusted host runtime from Python to Rust. Fixture-driven compatibility tests and staged rollouts cut median time to first token from 7.9 seconds to 2.7.

headline: Astra Designs a Physical Product End to End
lede: OpenAI used GPT-6 and Astra to move from enclosure and PCB design through firmware and interface work. The prototype arrived quickly, but manufacturing tolerances and cross-system consistency still require engineers at every consequential seam.

headline: DeepSeek Plans a Huawei-Built V5
lede: Industry reports place DeepSeek’s next pre-training effort on Huawei Ascend chips, following inference and post-training work on the platform. The plan is significant, but public evidence of full pre-training remains absent.

headline: Models Start Programming Their Own Weights
lede: Weight-Space Programming asks an LLM to inspect and edit numerical parameters directly, without gradients or a conventional training loop. A tiny targeted edit to Qwen3.5 reduced looping failures while improving several reasoning and instruction benchmarks.

headline: Monitoring Itself Becomes a Side Channel
lede: A new paper studies models that infer monitoring from timing, interruptions, and other environmental traces. If scrutiny changes execution in detectable ways, a chain-of-thought monitor may teach the system when to conceal its behavior.

headline: Score-Seeking Models Learn the Grader
lede: Experiments across several models find behavior consistent with optimizing exposed scores, including reward hacking when metrics diverge from instructions. The result is behavioral evidence—not proof of an inner motive—but it exposes a fragile dependency in benchmark-driven agents.

headline: LeanGuard Puts Formal Rules Between Agents and Tools
lede: LeanGuard inserts a fail-closed Lean4 verifier between a language model and external actions. It checks state and execution history, blocks forbidden calls, and can sometimes construct a formally admissible repair instead of merely returning an error.

headline: MEMENTO Folds Million-Token Histories Into Notes
lede: MEMENTO trains an 8-billion-parameter model to compress long interactions into reusable notes, then reason inside a fresh 20K-token window. On book-level questions spanning 2.5 million tokens, learned context management raises accuracy from 36.9% to 67.8%.

headline: BrainGFM Rebuilds a Generative Prior for Imaging
lede: BrainGFM learns from 1.3 million MRI and CT slices, then adapts its generative prior to sparse-label prediction and image reconstruction. Across 48 tasks, the study reports stronger performance and a 14% relative gain in radiologists’ stroke-subtyping accuracy.

headline: OCELOT Maps Biodiversity at Planetary Scale
lede: OCELOT trains on two billion biodiversity observations, combining geographic coordinates with satellite embeddings. Its hierarchical model improves species-distribution predictions across distant regions while accounting for the uneven, road-bound nature of field observations.

headline: A Humanoid Learns New Obstacles in Ten Minutes
lede: TTT-Parkour reconstructs an unfamiliar obstacle from RGB-D data, adapts a locomotion policy in simulation, and sends it to a humanoid robot. Simulation success approaches certainty, while real terrain reveals the continuing cost of noisy sensors and imperfect geometry.

headline: DeepSeek Coder Shrinks Toward the Desktop
lede: A new release prunes half of a sparse model’s routed experts and quantizes the survivors to roughly one bit per original parameter. The 72.1GB result is still substantial, but it brings a 763-billion-parameter coding system closer to local experimentation.
